#1673. Man United transfer news: Bruno Fernandes delivers big update on contract talks amid AC Milan links

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 12:16

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has claimed that it is 'not the right moment' to be talking about a new contract at Old Trafford.

Fernandes will lead out the Red Devils against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, with Mauricio Pochettino looking to mark his arrival at Old Trafford with a statement win.

Pochettino has confirmed that the Portuguese will remain as skipper, but reports emerged earlier this week that the playmaker is yet to accept an offer of a new deal.

Should Fernandes pen fresh terms at a time when Man United sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League table, it would represent a major boost for the club.

However, speaking in an interview with Sky Sports, Fernandes has suggested that he has no intention of committing his future to United anytime soon.

While Fernandes spoke positively over club officials making an attempt to extend his contract, he is keen to focus on matters on the pitch.

The former Sporting Lisbon star said: "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.

"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here."

He added: "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season.

"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games."

Unless Man United move clear of the Premier League relegation zone, it is highly unlikely that Fernandes will be signing a new contract.

That would make no sense for either party, regardless of Fernandes said to have admirers in AC Milan, who are managed by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

United can activate a 12-month option to protect their position, and that feels like the most realistic development over the coming months.

#1672. Juan Mata retires aged 38: Premier League legend calls time on glittering career as Manchester United pay tribute to former star

Published: 05:52 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 05:53 EST, 18 November 2026

Former Manchester United and Chelsea star Juan Mata has retired from football at the age of 38.

The Spain star, who came through Real Madrid's academy before winning the Champions League with Chelsea and the Europa League with both the Blues and Man United, enjoyed a dazzling career in England before moving to clubs in Turkey, Japan and Australia.

The midfielder also distinguished himself for his national side, winning the 2010 World Cup as part of the squad, and scoring in Spain's victorious Euro 2012 final against Italy.

Most recently featuring in Australia's A-League for Melbourne Victory, Mata announced the end of his playing career with a poignant video filmed inside a dressing room to the sound of Elvis Presley's 'Now or Never'.

In the clip, Mata symbolically hangs his boots on a hook in the locker room before leaving, with the video captioned: 'Sometimes, to love is to let go.

Sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq

Juan Mata has announced his retirement from football with a poignant video message (Source: Juan Mata)

The former Chelsea and Man United midfielder enjoyed a decorated career on English soil

A popular presence wherever he plied his trade, Mata's comments on social media were soon flooded with well-wishes from former clubs.

'Great player, better person,' Man United shared under his post on X. 'Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan (red heart emoji).'

Chelsea had a similar send-off for him, with the club writing: 'So many special memories. Thank you, Juan (blue heart emoji).'

Former Chelsea executive Marina Granovskaia added her personal thanks with a message too, writing: 'Great video! Great career too! (red heart emoji). Wishing you all the best Juan (blue heart emoji).'

Former team-mates including Ander Herrera, Ashley Young, Santi Cazorla and Mario Suarez were among those to send messages of thanks and congratulations, with Man City star Vivianne Miedema also writing to Mata.

'Congratulations on an amazing career and changing football on and off the pitch (hand clap emoji, green heart emoji),' the Dutch WSL trailblazer wrote.

Despite starting his youth career at Real Madrid, Mata's first senior minutes in the Spanish top flight came with his move in 2007 to Valencia.

Mata notched up 174 appearances for the side and won the Copa del Rey in club colours before his landmark move to Chelsea.

In west London, the midfielder won the FA Cup and Champions League in his first season, and the Europa League in his second.

The video contained a brief farewell message and was widely liked by his former team-mates

After leaving Chelsea, the Spaniard enjoyed a strong stint at Manchester United

At the end of last month, the Euro 2012 winner was treated to a lap of appreciation at his last club Melbourne Victory

But a falling-out with then-coach Jose Mourinho called time on his stint at Stamford Bridge and a move north to join Man United – where he would later reunite with the Portuguese manager during his stint in Manchester between 2016 and 2018.

Mata later enjoyed stints at Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before his move to Melbourne.

In recent years, however, Mata has expanded his career away from the pitch, with the player serving as a pundit at this year's World Cup for ITV, and at the 2024 European Championship for BBC Sport.

As well as appearing in the media, Mata is a keen investor in sporting ventures including Spanish club Real Oviedo, San Diego FC in the MLS and Formula One's Alpine racing team.

Alongside Italy icon Giorgio Chiellini, Mata is an investor in Mercury/13, a women's multi-club ownership group that invests in FC Como Women.

Mata is also a co-owner of Melbourne Victory, with plans to chair a football committee at the club after hanging up his boots.

As well as a shrewd businessman, Mata is also a philanthropist – and was recognised for his donations with an MBE in June 2025.

In 2017, Mata pledged one per cent of his salary to a charitable movement called Common Goal, which supports football charities.

#1670. Opinion: Liverpool eye move for perfect forward, they need him

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of players recently.

They have several areas among their ranks that need upgrading despite them spending well over £600 million on new players already.

This is obviously a major cause for concern but, right now, there isn't a lot that the Reds can do.

However, with the January transfer window now being just over a month away, some decisions are going to have to be made quickly.

Because, even though every section of Liverpool's first-team squad could do with improving, they don't have an endless amount of money to dip into.

So, that's why this latest move that they've been linked with could be perfect.

Gustavo Varela is constantly being scouted by Liverpool

One of Liverpool's main areas of focus that they've had over the last few years is their attack.

Everyone involved with the club knew that change was coming with Sadio Mane and Roberto Firmino already being shown the exit door.

However, the exit of Mohamed Salah was something that nobody could have anticipated, not after his performances the season prior, anyway.

But, the Egyptian King did end up leaving which has forced the Reds to spend well over £400 million on new attackers.

Some deals have worked out while others still have a lot to figure out.

But, right now, as per a fresh update from Corriere dello Sport, Gustavo Varela could be one of the players on top of Liverpool's shortlist.

"Napoli themselves have conducted a survey though not directly with Monza to try to anticipate the competition, which, in addition to Juventus, is fierce," they wrote.

"In the Premier League, Tottenham, Brentford, and Sunderland have inquired , while Liverpool sends scouts every week to monitor Varela's performance.

"The Serie A top scorer is also a hot topic abroad, but there's another factor: Benfica has a 20% interest in the future resale and the ability to match any offer that comes to the Monza club, having a preferential route. In other words, if a €40 million offer were to arrive, the Portuguese club could match it (in that case, the outlay would be € 32 million ) and bring home Gustavo Varela.

"It would still be a huge capital gain for the red and whites, given that they paid €2.5 million for him a few months ago, after he was close to joining Frosinone, who then preferred to invest in Tomas Bobcek, a mystery item in the Ciociaria's extraordinary start to the season."

Gustavo Varela would be a perfect back-up option for Liverpool

Right now, Liverpool only really have one proper number nine available to them.

Alexander Isak is their record signing and, while he's performed well, a lot more could be coming from the Sweden international.

Of course, Hugo Ekitike is going to return from injury in 2027 so he'll be able to take some pressure off Isak's shoulders but, since nobody knows how good the Frenchman is going to be upon his return, there could be a gap about to open up in Liverpool's squad.

Varela is a relatively unknown attacker but, right now, he's the Serie A's top goal scorer and he's easily Monza's best player.

Indeed, they may be sitting in the relegation zone at the moment but, with how well Varela is performing, they could find themselves out of the bottom three in no time.

Obviously, the transfer links with Liverpool are all just rumours for now but, if the club are sending scouts to watch him every week, they must be serious about wanting to invest in the Portuguese striker.

#1667. Manchester United braced for legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel: Insiders express concern for 16-year-old wonderkid's welfare amid fears of 'tapping up' by Spanish giants

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 06:43 EST, 18 November 2026

Manchester United have expressed their concern over the circumstances surrounding JJ Gabriel’s imminent move to Real Madrid, and threatened legal action if there is any evidence that he was induced to leave.

The 16-year-old winger posted a video on social media on Tuesday night confirming his departure from United as talks with Madrid continue between his new agent Ali Barat and close family at the club’s Valdebebas headquarters.

United sources say they are disappointed the video appeared without any contact with them, but the club will maintain its policy of not punishing Gabriel for what it sees as the actions of adults.

However, they have reiterated that United will fight with every legal means possible if any evidence of inducement from another club comes to light.

It’s understood that United have been unable to make contact with Gabriel – who has not been seen at the club since September – or his family despite numerous attempts to check on his welfare. They want an opportunity to ensure that he has a say in what could be a life-changing decision.

Gabriel has been training in Madrid and gave an interview to Marca earlier this month saying that he favoured a move to the 15-time European champions over rivals Barcelona, while expressing an ambition to win the Ballon d’Or.

Manchester United are prepared for a legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel

The youngster is on the verge of joining the Spanish giants in a controversial move

He is registered as a United player for the rest of the season and the club are refusing to tear up that agreement in the belief that he would still need approval from FIFA to make the move. However, sources stress that there has been no contact from any football authority seeking to de-register him.

Gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football. He is registered with United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.

There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.

In a farewell post on Instagram he said: 'Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.

'Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

'You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

'As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ.'

Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.

United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered his request to leave given he had become a key part of plans in first team training sessions this season

United were left rocked in September when Gabriel's family unexpectedly requested to cancel his contract with immediate effect.

Daily Mail Sport revealed at the time that United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered such a move given he had become a key part of plans in first team training sessions this season under Michael Carrick.

A week later, Daily Mail Sport revealed that the decline of United since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson was the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

'His dad has ambitions for his son to be the best in the world and play with the best and learn from the best and right now that's not current situation at United - far from it,' a source explained.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under 21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah.

#1666. Opinion: Liverpool will sign their own N'Golo Kante

Liverpool's midfield has needed upgrading for a while now.

Ryan Gravenberch, Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni are the four options that Andoni Iraola has at his disposal right now.

Indeed, James McConnell has also made a couple of appearances but, he's more of a back-up option in case three of the other four central midfielders are injured.

Fans have known that ever since Fabinho left, they've needed to sign a new number six.

And, because that hasn't happened yet, their title rivals have managed to get even further away from them.

Many different rumours and links have emerged over the last couple of years but now, the Reds' very own version of N'Golo Kante could be on his way to Anfield.

Liverpool have tabled a €70m bid for Lamine Camara

Defensive-midfield is the main position that Liverpool need to upgrade right now.

Even though the Anfield outfit have also got to sign players in other positions, midfield should be their next area of focus.

During the summer, several different players emerged as potential options for Liverpool but, one player who kept popping up was Lamine Camara.

The Senegalese midfielder has quickly become one of AS Monaco's most important players and, he's only 22 years old.

Indeed, he's never played outside of Ligue 1 before but, if he hits the ground running like Mamadou Sangare did for Brentford, the Reds will be onto a winner.

That's why this latest update from journalist Ekrem Konur is rather exciting.

"Having tracked AS Monaco's 22-year-old Senegalese midfielder Lamine Camara for months, Liverpool have tabled a massive €70 million bid to land their top target," he wrote.

Lamine Camara will become Liverpool's own N'Golo Kante

N'Golo Kante was probably one of the Premier League's best defensive midfielders over the last 10 or so years.

The Frenchman managed to win the Premier League title twice and he even added a World Cup to his trophy cabinet back in 2018.

Obviously, he's now playing for Fenerbahce in the Turkish Super Lig but, at 35 years old, it's clear that he's coming to the end of his career.

Camara, on the other hand, is only just getting started with his and, right now, he's one of the most talked-about players in the world.

In fact, his performances have been that impressive that some people haveeven compared his skillset to Kante's .

The €70 million fee now required to sign Camara is obviously a bit of a stumbling block but, right now, it feels like the 22-year-old is their best option.

Here's hoping that Liverpool can strike a deal for him in January, otherwise, they could end up falling even further behind their title rivals.

With top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

Moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

The pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

Alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

Primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

Finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

#1664. Spurs transfer news: Can Mikey Moore be recalled from FC Koln in January?

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 13:07

Tottenham Hotspur allegedly do not have the option to recall Mikey Moore from his loan at FC Koln.

Spurs' 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town on Saturday afternoon has moved the club into ninth place in the Premier League table.

With a squad possessing depth and a schedule that lacks European football, Roberto De Zerbi is not exactly in desperate need of additions during the winter transfer window.

Nevertheless, academy graduate Moore is earning regular football in Germany, seemingly putting him in the thoughts of the Italian.

However, as per talkSPORT, Spurs may have to wait until the summer to reintegrate the winger.

Moore made the headlines on Friday courtesy of scoring for FC Koln against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga.

The 19-year-old's early effort at the Allianz Arena helped earn his side a 1-1 draw against the champions.

That goal was Moore's first in six starts and three substitute outings in Germany's top flight.

Nevertheless, Spurs are seemingly not in the position to automatically recall Moore should they wish to do so.

With Moore having already represented Spurs this season, he can only play for his parent club or Koln for the remainder of the campaign.

If Spurs earn a return to European football for 2027-28, Moore's homegrown status means that he will likely be used in De Zerbi's squad.

For now, though, it makes sense that he is playing a key role for Koln, who sit in 13th place in the Bundesliga table.

Should he continue to accumulate regular minutes, it will stand him in good stead for next season.

#1663. Report: Rivals step up chase for Liverpool's best January target

Although Liverpool have spent £650 million since winning the Premier League in 2025, they are still competing for some of Europe's most exciting players.

Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak both arrived for then-British record transfer fees in the summer of 2025, and Bradley Barcola arrived this summer to become Liverpool's third £110 million+ signing.

The Reds' forward line still isn't complete though, and Andoni Iraola's side are reportedly looking to bring in another attacker.

Whether a move comes this winter or in the summer isn't yet clear, but potential targets are still being discussed in the run up to the January window.

Liverpool will face competition though, including from one Premier League rival.

Liverpool and Arsenal to battle for sensational wingerAntonio Nusa has been one of Europe's best forwards this season, displaying some truly sensational form for RB Leipzig. With 15 goal involvements in his first 16 matches, the Norwegian has proven himself as an elite forward despite only being 21-years-old. His emergence as one of Europe's best has been met with plenty of excitement from club's around the continent, including Liverpool, and a big move seems to be in the pipeline. Liverpool aren't the only team interested from the Premier League though, with Arsenal reportedly readying a move for Nusa.

Antonio Nusa has been one of Europe's best forwards this season, displaying some truly sensational form for RB Leipzig.

With 15 goal involvements in his first 16 matches, the Norwegian has proven himself as an elite forward despite only being 21-years-old.

His emergence as one of Europe's best has been met with plenty of excitement from club's around the continent, including Liverpool, and a big move seems to be in the pipeline.

Liverpool aren't the only team interested from the Premier League though, with Arsenal reportedly readying a move for Nusa.

#1662. Slovan Bratislava vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 13:13

Slovan Bratislava will be looking to secure their first victory of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign when they host Real Betis at Tehelne Pole Stadion on Tuesday.

The Sky Blues sit bottom of the league phase table with no points from four matches, while Betis occupy 11th place with nine points.

Slovan defeated Celje away from home in the second leg of their playoff-round tie to secure a place in the Champions League main phase, marking a historic achievement for the club.

However, the Slovakian side have found the step up in quality difficult to handle, losing all four of their matches, scoring just once and conceding 17 goals.

Yaya Toure's side began their campaign with a heavy 6-1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain before suffering further losses against Stuttgart, Roma and LASK.

Balancing their domestic and European commitments has also proved challenging, with their continental struggles seemingly affecting their league form, as they sit second in the Slovakian top flight, seven points behind leaders DAC 1904 despite having played a game more.

Perhaps most frustrating for Toure is Slovan's poor home form, with the Sky Blues winless in their last five matches at Tehelne Pole Stadion, drawing three of those encounters.

Real Betis have made a solid start to their European campaign, collecting three wins from four matches while scoring eight goals and conceding six.

El Glorioso opened their campaign with a hard-fought 3-2 victory over Lille, coming from behind to claim all three points.

They followed that up with another thrilling 3-2 win against Porto before beating Feyenoord 1-0 to secure back-to-back home victories.

Manuel Pellegrini's side suffered a narrow 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in their previous Champions League outing, but they have an excellent opportunity to climb the table with a victory over Slovan.

Betis are unbeaten in their last three matches across all competitions and head into this encounter on the back of a 1-1 draw against city rivals Sevilla.

Slovan Bratislava form (all competitions):

The switch from a 3-4-3 to a 4-1-4-1 formation has helped Slovan pick up a draw and a victory in their last two matches, and Toure is likely to stick with the same system.

The back four of Sandro Cruz, Svetozar Markovic, Kenan Bajric and Daiki Matsuoka are expected to retain their places, with Peter Pokorny operating at the base of midfield.

Artur Gajdos appeared to pick up an injury in the previous game and could be replaced by Alexej Maros, while Andraz Sporar is set to continue up front, with Roman Cerepaki a doubt due to a back problem.

Real Betis are likely to be without Dani Ceballos, who is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem and is not expected to return to action before the start of December.

Fran Garcia and Hector Bellerin are expected to retain their places in defence, while Diego Llorente could come into the side in place of Marc Bartra.

Antony picked up a knock in the derby but he has travelled with the squad, and should retain his place alongside Isco and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli, with Jose Antonio Morante currently sidelined through injury.

Slovan Bratislava possible starting lineup:

Popovic; Cruz, Markovic, Bajric, Matsuoka; Pokomy, Barseghyan, Ibrahim, Maros, Marcelli, Sporar

Valles; Garcia, Natan, Llorente, Bellerin; Fornals, Bernal; Ezzalzouli, Isco, Antony; Parrott

Slovan have looked like fish out of water in the Champions League this season, and it would take a herculean effort for them to get anything from this encounter, although we expect the hosts to put up a better fight.

Real Betis, meanwhile, have been flying in Europe this season and should be confident of securing their second away victory in the competition as they look to bounce back from their defeat against Dortmund.

#1661. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Danns.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

Aston Villa have been told their Champions League clash with Galatasaray on Tuesday will still take place at the home of the Turkish champions despite the worrying state of the pitch.

UEFA Article 5 states: ‘The field of play must be smooth and level and comply with the IFAB Laws of the Game.’

Villa will look to strengthen their position in the league phase after winning three of their opening four games, though they lost their last fixture, at Barcelona.

Galatasaray are working around the clock to ensure their pitch is up to standard for their Champions League clash against Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom)

Unai Emery’s men have already beaten Turkish opposition this term, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 for their record European win, though that fixture was at Villa Park.

After the chaotic 4-4 draw at Manchester United before the international break, Villa meet Sunderland at home in the Premier League on Saturday.

Emery has doubts over Matty Cash and Johan Manzambi, who picked up injuries while on international duty and may struggle to recover in time.

#1659. GdS: ‘If not the best’ – Cardinale accelerates by publicly declaring Milan’s Endrick admiration

A rather significant step was taken on Saturday, as Gerry Cardinale publicly declared AC Milan’s interest in signing Endrick.

La Gazzetta dello Sport have revealed that Cardinale spent six hours at Milanello yesterday, after four at Casa Milan. The owner fully immersed himself in the Milan world again: he spoke with his transfer team, with the team about the match against Frosinone, and with Ruben Amorim about both topics.

While Cardinale did not confirm the imminent arrival of Markus Krösche – though he did admit to being in talks with him – his clear intention is to build a top-tier organisation. Cardinale’s goal is to lead Milan to a trophy – ideally the Scudetto – as early as this season.

To do this, he knows strengthening the squad in January is a necessity. One name stands out in his notebook: Endrick, the forward currently with Real Madrid whom Mourinho – for the time being – is unwilling to let go of.

Regarding a potential move for the 20-year-old, Cardinale confirmed that the club like him: “Endrick’s name keeps coming up in the market. Our project goes beyond any single player, but Endrick is one of the best in the world – if not the best – considering his age and position. I have enormous respect for him, and we’ll see what might be possible.”

In other words, the green light would need to be secured from Mourinho regarding his departure from Madrid. Milan know they can leverage the strong relationship between its owner and Roc Nation, the agency representing the Brazilian.

Given the business already conducted between RedBird and Roc Nation, it is likely that the player would favour Milan over other potential destinations. Meanwhile, Tresoldi has also piqued Cardinale’s interest, though he offers a different profile than Endrick.

Nicolo Tresoldi is also an option for the attack, but more significant progress has been made regarding the Brazilian. Bayern Munich are also watching the Club Brugge striker, with Harry Kane having undergone ankle surgery.

In any case, Milan’s transfer activity will not be limited to a striker. Further arrivals will depend on the opportunities that arise during the winter window, with agents and intermediaries continually ringing the phone lines at Casa Milan.

There is a desire to bolster the defence, potentially with a central defender (possibly through the early return of Zachary Athekame, currently on loan at Lyon) and a left-sided player, should Pervis Estupiñán be sold.

All of this is in addition to the contract renewal for Rabiot, the next player set to be secured following the agreements reached with Strahinja Pavlović and Christian Pulišić. In short, there is a lot in the works.

#1658. Report: Liverpool eyeing move for €45m left-back, it's not Alejandro Balde

Alejandro Balde has been one of the most linked players with Liverpool since the summer transfer window slammed shut.

Before the 2026-27 season fully kicked off, nobody realised that the Reds would already be needing a new left-back.

Fans, pundits and journalists all thought that Milos Kerkez would step up to the plate and make a huge improvement on his game now that Andy Robertson has left.

However, the opposite seems to have happened with neither Kerkez nor Kostas Tsimikas meeting expectations.

This poor form has led to many transfer rumours emerging and now, yet another left-back has been added to Liverpool's shortlist.

Liverpool are in the running for Daniel Svensson

As mentioned, left-back has been a major problem area for Liverpool this term.

The rest of their back four have performed fairly well with some such as Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo even being considered as Liverpool's signings of the season.

Balde felt like the most likely candidate to make the switch, especially since Barcelona only want around €40 million to allow him to leave.

However, with so many other clubs also vying for the transfer of the Spaniard, they need to have alternative options to explore, just in case.

So, that's why this latest update from FussballNews is rather exciting.

"According to information from fussball-news.de, Liverpool and Arsenal from the Premier League are showing the greatest interest, while Manchester United and Leeds United are also keeping a close eye on the player," they wrote.

"It is said that the scouting team of the 'Red Devils' observed him in the Champions League game against Real Betis and produced a report with the rating 'transferable/signable'".

"According to information from fussball-news.de, the management of Borussia Dortmund is still committed to keeping Svensson – who has a long-term contract running until June 2029 – and does not want to let him leave.

"Whether the club completely closes its doors depends on the conditions put on the table. While the club doesn't consider the player untouchable, it is reluctant to let him go unless suitable conditions are met and plans to strengthen its commitment through a salary increase.

"Borussia Dortmund are hoping for at least €45 million if a sale goes through. Should competition intensify, the total package, including add-ons, could potentially reach €50 million, with performance-related bonuses and sell-on clauses likely to be decisive factors in any deal.

"Premier League clubs are reportedly prepared to test his situation with a €30 million offer for the Swedish player. However, the player is said to be happy in Dortmund and not planning a hasty move."

Daniel Svensson would be a smart transfer for Liverpool

Liverpool's defence has obviously been one of their main areas of focus when improving their ranks over the last couple of years.

After Araujo and Jacquet were brought in, most people thought that they'd be set for a while.

However, with Araujo's future still undecided and their left-backs failing to perform, it feels like Liverpool are going to have to focus a lot of their attention on their defence again.

Of all the left-backs linked with a Liverpool move, Svensson and Balde are the two most likely deals to be sanctioned with the former of the two regularly linked with a move in the past.

Both players are young and have a lot of their careers left ahead of them and, in the current transfer market, the €40 million - €50 million they they'd cost seem to be fairly cheap.

Obviously, neither of them have played in the Premier League before so, both players would be risky purchases but, looking back at their performances from the last couple of seasons, it feels like they'd both fit straight into Iraola's plans and help Liverpool out massively.

#1656. Newcastle United transfer news: Surprise Nick Woltemade swap deal with Magpies 'interested' in Juventus attacker

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 13:39

Newcastle United are reportedly interested in negotiating a swap deal with Juventus involving Nick Woltemade.

The Magpies earned a spirited 2-2 draw with leaders Arsenal on Saturday evening to end the day in 12th position in the Premier League table.

However, with just three wins in 11 league matches, Matthias Jaissle remains under pressure at St James' Park.

During the summer transfer window, the decision was taken to allow Woltemade to move on loan to Juventus.

That is despite Newcastle having paid £69m for the forward during the 2025 summer transfer window.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Newcastle chiefs are open-minded to allowing the Germany international to remain in Turin on a permanent basis.

Nevertheless, it is claimed that they would like to discuss a potential swap deal involving Francisco Conceicao.

That is despite the Portuguese winger said to remain as a favourite of Juve boss Luciano Spalletti.

Conceicao has contributed just one goal and one assist from his seven starts and two substitute outings in Serie A and the Europa League.

If Juventus wish to keep Woltemade on a permanent basis, they will need to generate funds or go down the player-exchange route.

Newcastle will not consider selling Woltemade for less than £50m, a figure that Juventus cannot meet at the present time.

Unless the Premier League club take an interest in another Juventus player, the Italian club may have to be open-minded to allowing Conceicao to leave, assuming that Woltemade's return in the final third is viewed more important.

#1655. Report: Real Madrid could now decide Liverpool star's future

Liverpool's squad has undergone several massive changes since winning the Premier League in 2025.

The team that Arne Slot inherited from Jurgen Klopp has now been dismantled, and a series of big money additions have formed the core of Andoni Iraola's current team.

Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola became the first trio to all cost over £100 million to be fielded at the same time this season, and more big changes are on the horizon at Anfield.

A number of the Reds' established stars are being linked with exits as Iraola continues to find his feet, and an update has now been given on one contract standoff.

Alexis Mac Allister made his disappointment at not being offered a new deal this summer very clear.

The World Cup winner went public with his feelings early in the season and has delivered some very impressive performances on the pitch since.

Uncertainty around the midfielder's future has led to an increase in links to a move away, with Real Madrid one of the teams most interested in Mac Allister.

A new report from Football Insider has revealed that the Argentine is using the interest from Los Blancos to leverage his position when negotiating a new deal with the Reds.

After Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch were recently rewarded with new deals, Mac Allister is believed to be sticking strictly to his demands, and Real Madrid's position could decide his future.

If the Spanish giants are legitimately interested in bringing in the Argentine midfielder, then Liverpool may decide to cash in rather than paying out to sign the 27-year-old to an extended deal.

With a contract running through to 2028, the Reds are under no immediate pressure to sell Mac Allister but, if no new deal looks likely in the summer, then a sale would make a lot of sense.

Real Madrid's interest in Mac Allister looks likely to decide his future, and the midfielder may be playing in white rather than red sooner rather than later.

#1652. The wild life of Peter Storey who died aged 81: An Arsenal double-winning legend who was jailed for three years for his role in a criminal counterfeit operation, once ran a brothel and was caught trying to smuggle adult films into the UK

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list

Joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an important part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010)

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

#1651. Everton targeting Iceland international as Thierno Barry alternative

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could make signing a new centre-forward a priority in January after entering the season short of options in attack.

David Moyes needs additional firepower to strengthen his squad, and a promising Iceland international has reportedly emerged as a potential solution.

Real Sociedad striker Orri Oskarsson is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, with Everton understood to be paying particularly close attention to his progress.

The 22-year-old has impressed in Spain, and the Toffees could explore a move as they look to address a key weakness in their squad.

According to TEAMtalk, Everton are among the clubs monitoring Oskarsson ahead of the January transfer window. Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Brentford are also reportedly tracking the Icelandic forward, meaning Moyes could face competition if Everton decide to pursue a deal.

Everton’s need for a striker has become increasingly apparent following their summer business. Beto departed for Fiorentina without a replacement arriving, leaving Thierno Barry as the club’s only recognised centre-forward. Attempts to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco and Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United also failed to produce a deal.

That situation has reportedly encouraged Everton to examine their options ahead of January, with Oskarsson among the forwards attracting attention.

The Iceland international joined Real Sociedad from FC Copenhagen in 2024 and made progress during his previous campaign, scoring nine goals in LaLiga. His combination of physical presence, technical ability and finishing has helped establish him as an appealing prospect for clubs looking to strengthen their attacking ranks.

Oskarsson has also continued to impress at international level, with his performances for Iceland adding to his growing reputation. At 22, he could offer Everton both an immediate option up front and a potential long-term investment.

However, Everton would need to establish whether Real Sociedad are prepared to negotiate during the January window. The Spanish club invested significantly to secure his services, and there is no confirmation that they would be willing to let him leave midway through the season.

Oskarsson could be an important addition for Everton as Moyes looks to address the lack of depth at centre-forward. Relying heavily on Barry leaves the manager with limited specialist alternatives, particularly across a demanding second half of the campaign.

The Icelandic striker’s profile could suit Everton’s need for another option capable of leading the line. His technical qualities may also give Moyes greater flexibility in how the team approaches matches, while his age offers scope for further development.

Competition from Tottenham, Newcastle, Sunderland and Brentford could complicate Everton’s pursuit, however. The Toffees would need to move decisively if their interest develops into a formal approach, while the final cost and Sociedad’s willingness to sell would be key factors.

For now, Everton’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing potential solutions ahead of January rather than confirming a deal is imminent. With Moyes needing greater depth in attack, Oskarsson is a name to watch as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1650. TMW: A ‘try-out’ at San Siro – Milan to watch Frosinone star up close amid interest

Gabriele Calvani is expected to start for Frosinone against AC Milan at San Siro, and it could be an audition of sorts.

TMW report that the game will be a chance for Calvani to show off his qualities, especially in front of those who are following him closely in view of the winter. Milan’s management will watch the defender up close, who is currently owned by Genoa and on loan to the Ciociaria.

He has been added to the Rossoneri’s list of potential reinforcements. In recent weeks, Milan representatives have been watching Frosinone, also to closely evaluate the Italy U21 international. After leaving the Azzurrini training camp with a hamstring problem, the defender will start tonight.

#1649. Bromley vs Wycombe Wanderers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 22 Nov 2026 15:14, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 15:14

Bromley will be looking to pick up another victory when they welcome Wycombe Wanderers to the CopperJax Community Stadium on Tuesday evening.

The hosts currently sit 23rd in the League One table, while the visitors are 15th.

Bromley finally ended their woeful run of form on Saturday, securing a hugely important 1-0 victory away to promotion contenders Reading.

Victor Adeboyejo scored the only goal of the game and goalkeeper Shamal George made a host of impressive save to help the Ravens claim all three points.

That win ended a run of 10 games without a victory across all competitions and was Karl Robinson's first since he replaced Andy Woodman as head coach earlier this month.

It also saw Bromley move off the foot of the table, leaving them just one point from safety.

However, they do have the worst defensive record in the division, having conceded 33 goals in 14 games so far.

Wycombe, meanwhile, will be looking to bounce back from a disappointing defeat to Oxford United on Saturday.

The Chairboys suffered a remarkable 4-3 loss despite the fact they were 3-0 ahead going into the final 20 minutes.

Goals from Jayden Wareham, Malik Mothersille and Aaron Morley had put Wycombe in a commanding position, but Oxford scored four late goals to pick up a stunning victory.

Tom Hounsell's side also ended the game with nine men after Dan Casey and Luke Leahy were sent off.

Hounsell admitted the defeat was a "bitter pill to swallow", but felt his side "dominated the game" for 70 minutes and must take heart from that.

Wycombe Wanderers form (all competitions):

Bromley could hand Adeboyejo a start after he scored off the bench against Reading, with Michael Cheek set to drop to the bench.

Jodi Jones and Mickel Miller could continue out wide, with Kamil Conteh and George Saville set to start in midfield.

Wycombe will be without Casey and Leahy, with the pair suspended following their red cards against Oxford.

Steve Cook is set to replace Casey in defence, while Wareham is expected to continue up front.

George; Ifill, Oxford, Taylor, Mendy; Jones, Conteh, Saville, Miller; Adeboyejo, Pinnock

Wycombe Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Hazard; Grimmer, Cook, Taylor, Hagelskjaer; Morley, Scowen; Thomas, Boyd-Munce, Mothersille; Wareham

Bromley will be full of confidence after beating Reading and we are backing them to pick up a point against a Wycombe side that capitulated in dramatic fashion against Oxford.
